profile.title: Full-Stack Developer
profile.introduction: I'm a full-stack developer who enjoys the parts of the job that are invisible when they go well: clean API boundaries, data models that still make sense a year later, and interfaces that stay usable at 3am on a phone with one bar of signal.
profile.philosophy: Write the simplest thing that is genuinely correct, then make it fast only where measurement says it matters. Code is read far more often than it is written, so clarity beats cleverness almost every time. Anything that has to be remembered will eventually be forgotten, so encode it in types, tests or constraints instead.
profile.currentFocus: Deepening my work on distributed systems fundamentals, and getting better at designing APIs that stay pleasant to use as they grow.
profile.careerSummary: Around five years building web applications across agency, logistics and analytics teams — most recently leading the redesign of a customer-facing reporting API, and consistently the person who ends up owning data modelling and API contracts.

projects.title: BM Canteen
projects.shortDescription: A full-stack portfolio with a REST API, JWT-authenticated admin panel and a swappable persistence layer.
projects.description: A production-shaped portfolio application rather than a static site. The public pages render entirely from the API, and every piece of content — projects, skills, experience, education and the About copy — is editable through an authenticated admin panel. The persistence layer sits behind a repository interface, so the storage backend can be replaced without touching a controller, a service or a single line of frontend code.
projects.problem: Static portfolio sites prove that someone can style a page. They prove nothing about API design, authentication, data modelling or how a person structures an application that has to be maintained. Every content change also means a code change and a redeploy.
projects.solution: Split the application into a React frontend and an Express REST API with a layered backend: routes delegate to controllers, controllers to services, and services to repositories behind an interface. Content lives in the database and is managed through a protected admin panel, so updating a job title is an admin action rather than a deploy.
features: JWT authentication delivered in an httpOnly cookie with CSRF double-submit protection
Full CRUD for projects, experience, education, skills and technologies
Paginated, filterable contact-message inbox with unread/read/archived states
Light, dark and system themes with the preference persisted
Repository layer allowing the storage backend to be swapped in isolation
Centralised error handling with a consistent response envelope
projects.architecture: React and Axios talk to an Express REST API. Requests pass through helmet, CORS, rate limiting, authentication and express-validator before reaching a thin controller, which delegates to a service holding the business logic. Services depend only on repository interfaces, so the concrete storage implementation is injected at a single composition root.
projects.challenges: Keeping the storage layer genuinely swappable meant resisting the temptation to leak query objects through the repository interface. Filters are expressed in domain vocabulary instead, which required designing purpose-built repository methods rather than one generic find().
projects.lessonsLearned: Cross-entity rules belong in the service layer, not in schema validators. Pushing date-ordering and uniqueness checks up one level meant they held for every storage backend rather than only the one that happened to be wired up.

projects.title: Loyaltri-HRMS
projects.shortDescription: A multi-user kanban board with live cursors, optimistic updates and conflict resolution over WebSockets.
projects.description: A collaborative planning board where several people can drag cards simultaneously and see each other work in real time. The interesting part is not the board — it is reconciling concurrent edits without the UI flickering or losing a change.
projects.problem: Naive realtime boards either lock a card while someone drags it, which feels broken, or apply every event blindly, which means two people moving the same card produce an inconsistent result.
projects.solution: Optimistic local updates paired with a server-authoritative event log. Each mutation carries a client id and a monotonic sequence number, so late-arriving events can be reordered or discarded rather than blindly replayed.
features: Offline queueing with replay on reconnect
projects.architecture: A Socket.IO gateway sits alongside the REST API and shares its authentication middleware. Board state is held in Redis for fast fan-out, with periodic snapshots to the primary database.
projects.challenges: Reconnection was harder than the realtime path itself. A client that drops mid-drag must replay queued mutations without duplicating them, which meant making every mutation idempotent.
projects.lessonsLearned: Designing events to be idempotent from the start is far cheaper than retrofitting deduplication once the protocol is in use.

projects.title: Inventory Forecasting API
projects.shortDescription: A REST service that projects stock depletion from historical sales and flags reorder points.
projects.description: A backend service for small retailers that turns raw sales history into actionable reorder dates. Built API-first, with a scheduled job recomputing forecasts nightly and a thin dashboard consuming the same public endpoints.
projects.problem: Small retailers discover they are out of stock when a customer asks. Spreadsheets do not account for lead time or seasonal variation, so reorders are consistently late.
projects.solution: A weighted moving average over trailing sales, adjusted for per-supplier lead time, producing a projected depletion date per SKU. Anything inside its lead-time window is surfaced as a reorder alert.
features: Bulk CSV import with per-row validation and error reporting
projects.architecture: Express REST API over PostgreSQL, with a scheduled worker recomputing forecasts out of band so request latency is unaffected by the heavier statistical work.
projects.challenges: CSV import was the source of most real-world failures. Reporting every bad row at once, rather than failing on the first, turned a frustrating loop into a single correction pass.
projects.lessonsLearned: Validation feedback quality matters more than validation strictness. Users abandon an import that rejects their file without saying which of 4,000 rows was wrong.

experience.description: Lead engineer on a customer-facing analytics product. Redesigned the reporting API around cursor pagination, cutting p95 response time from 1.8s to 240ms. Introduced a shared component library that removed roughly 6,000 lines of duplicated UI code across three applications, and mentored two engineers through their first production services.

Built and maintained internal tooling for a logistics platform handling around 40,000 shipments a day. Replaced a nightly batch reconciliation job with an event-driven pipeline, reducing data staleness from 24 hours to under a minute. Owned the migration from JavaScript to TypeScript across four services.

Delivered client web applications in a small agency team. Introduced automated accessibility testing into the build pipeline, which took the default project template from repeated WCAG failures to AA conformance at handover.
Supported an undergraduate web development module of around 120 students, running lab sessions on HTTP, REST design and relational modelling, and marking coursework.

education.description: Final-year project built a distributed task scheduler with at-least-once delivery guarantees. Coursework covered algorithms, databases, operating systems, computer networks and human-computer interaction.
Part-time certificate covering container orchestration, infrastructure as code, observability and deployment strategy.
Ongoing study of WCAG 2.2 criteria, assistive technology behaviour and accessible design patterns.
